newsitem.title: POLAND: Protest at Polish refinery, production unaffected.
newsitem.headline: Protest at Polish refinery, production unaffected.

text.p: Trade unions in Poland's second biggest refinery, Rafineria Gdanska SA, staged a one-hour protest action on Friday but production was not affected, the company's spokeswoman said.

"The protest was quiet. State and unions' flags were put up ...which did not influence the company's work," Ewa Sielicka told Reuters. The refinery's workers are protesting against the government's failure to offer them free shares in the firm.
The Gdansk refinery's largest shareholder is the state-owned oil holding Nafta Polska SA, which has 75 percent of shares.
The unions demand 15 percent of shares for free, which they say they should get in line with the new privatisation law which comes into force on April 8.

The unions' protest, originally planned as a one-hour warning work stoppage, was scaled down after the workers received a letter from Nafta Polska in which the holding recognized their right to receive the shares soon after the new law is in place.
